neighbours.label: word that opens a fixed idiom whose next word is near-certain: 'go' in 'can't go [wrong]', 'half' in 'half [way] / half [my age]', 'pronounced' in 'pronounced [dead]'
fire: For a birthday present, you honestly can't go wrong with a good book.
By noon we were about half way to the summit.
The driver was pronounced dead shortly after the crash.
With a classic white shirt, you will never go wrong at a wedding.
The runner beside me was nearly half my age.
After a long fight the patient was pronounced dead at midnight.
If you choose any of these three hotels, you really cannot go wrong.
I'm only half way through the second season of the show.
quiet: For a birthday present, we decided to go to a bookstore downtown.
By noon we had eaten half of the sandwiches.
The driver pronounced the street name with a heavy accent.
With a classic white shirt, you can go to most weddings.
The runner beside me drank half a bottle of water.
After a long fight the patient went home at midnight.
If you choose any of these three hotels, you can go there by train.
I'm watching the second season of the show with my sister.

notes: The + pole fires on 'start' / 'to be [sure]' and promotes adjectives; the - pole is the same 'predictable continuation' slot for idioms. Near misses keep the words in literal use (probe: 'go to the market' 0.17, 'cut in half' 0.08).
